title: Why the insights show a rate, not a total

steps.say: This block is the whole argument of the page. It holds an amount per learner per week — a rate — and never a running total.
A total only ever says how big and how old something is, so a large school beats a small one before anybody has done a thing. A rate says how fast it is moving, which is the part you can act on.

Your level's rate sits beside whatever you are comparing it to, and the line above says in words what the current measure counts. Change the **window** and the same rate is computed over a shorter or a longer period.
steps.terminal: A pace matters more than a position — a class three sentences behind but climbing fast is healthier than one parked far ahead. This tour changed nothing; only your own taps do.
